title: Insufficient Manpower
text: We continued our circus tour and slave trading business, indeed. Time passed in this fashion, and Big Sister's friends had mostly all been recovered. While we waited for Queen's return, the time for the second wave drew steadily nearer. As for what I was doing during that time, I went to see Filolial Sage to have him look after Yuki-chan and the others. Given the timing, I was rather anxious that the Crimson Swine might be in the process of stealing Fleon-chan's egg from Sage, so I made sure to arrange things a bit earlier than usual.

What I'd learned across these loops was that Sage's thinking leaned somewhat toward Melromarc's side, while at the same time he was the sort of man who cherished Filolial-sama above all. He was of a moderate temperament, but seemed to have some difficulty with feelings toward demi-humans and beastmen. Of course he didn't approve of abuse or anything of that sort—he simply found them a bit frightening while treasuring Filolial-sama all the more. That was the kind of man he was.

This time around, we introduced ourselves as running a circus with Filolial-sama, and grew close to him through Yuki-chan's supposed interest in racing, and thus were granted Fleon-chan's egg. Since we'd extended an invitation on behalf of the more peaceful branch of the circus on Zeltoble's side, we secured a promise that he'd come watch once everything was settled. And so, we brought Fleon-chan's egg back home.
“Oh, did you buy another Filolial egg, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Isn't that a bit much?”
“Don't you dare try to make more Lunas.”
Itsuki and Ren scolded me thus, but I paid them no mind.
“This little one is Fleon-chan, I say. Same as Filo-tan, it's about time to start preparing to secure and raise her properly.”
“Oh, does that mean there's some special way you have to raise her?”
“You could say that, but how should I put this…”
“If you want to keep things consistent with before, it would be wise to follow the same pattern without deviation,” Rafumi chimed in, poking her face in.

Yes yes, I understood that already. But surely Fleon-chan didn't need her circumstances reproduced quite so precisely as Filo-tan's had been? Or so I thought. Even when the timing was off, Fleon-chan had still turned out to be Fleon-chan, hadn't she?
“Well, I do intend to fix the timing and match the food given as closely as possible. But in the previous loop, though the timing was different, Fleon-chan turned out the same regardless, I say.”
In that previous loop, the wave problem had already been resolved by that point in time. Even then, Fleon-chan had shown no change. Itsuki had put up quite a fight about it.
“By my calculations, the judgment is that wave monsters must be mixed into the feed. You may refuse, Spear Hero, but tell me—have you ever done things differently across these loops?”

“Guh…” Vexing as it was, it was true that we'd had Fleon-chan hatch during wave season and eat what was gained during that time. It might well be a necessary element drawn from Filo-tan's circumstance reproduction. Even the case of Luna-chan turning out white was backed up by Rafumi's calculations, after all.
“I suppose that makes her a special kind of Filolial, but what sort of girl is she?”
“The secret of Fleon, the first Filolial the Spear Hero ever raised, is—”
Rafumi was being suggestive again. Father, Ren, and Itsuki all decided to ignore her rather than play along.
“Oi. If you don't listen properly, I'll cause mischief.”
“You really are a bothersome person.”
“That's just who I am! Come now, listen closely. I'll make a special exception and tell you this time.”
“You never say anything unprompted otherwise!”
“That's why I'm saying I'll answer you now. Listen.”
“Yeah, yeah. So what kind of thing is this Fleon?”
“Ah, the one I gave to Spear Hero already knows, and since some of it's already been discussed, Yuki probably has some vague idea—she's a flying Filolial.”
That Rafumi, blabbing away so freely.
“Ohh… isn't that amazing? Oh, so there are Filolials that can fly?”
“They're extinct, as it happens. But using this one's factor, it's possible to make Filolials fly even through acquired means. She's the key Filolial for that.”
“That's incredible.”
“If she can fly, wouldn't that make a great circus attraction?”
“I won't be putting Fleon-chan on display, I say. I promised Sage as much.”

I'd already explained about the circus business. But before accepting her, I'd declared to Sage that I would absolutely never make a spectacle of Fleon-chan's flying. Sage cared about many things regarding Fleon-chan, and he'd been worried about her being used for such purposes. Of course I'd respect Fleon-chan's own will, but flying would never, under any circumstances, be turned into a show. Though I was quite displeased to have learned it from Rival, a flying Filolial-sama represented a technique that any Filolial-sama could in principle achieve.
“Still, seems a waste not to use it, if you ask me.”
“Bit rich of you to keep Keel and me as attractions while refusing to do the same with her.”
“Ren, you really hold onto grudges too much.”
“Shut up.”
“So, is flying all she can do?”
“Oh no. This is a genuinely interesting Filolial once she meets you, Bow Hero. I can guarantee that much. Raf-raf-raf, you'd best look forward to it.”
“Doesn't sound like it'll end well.”
“That was oddly cryptic… well, whatever.”
The time to begin raising Fleon-chan was drawing near.

“Changing the subject, but the wave is getting close, isn't it? Seems like there's a lot of movement happening within Melromarc—apparently they're strengthening conscription, and villages and towns everywhere are getting restless.”
“Isn't that only natural, given it's a crisis facing the whole world?”
“I suppose you could say that, but— this is from Rafumi-chan, who's been acting as Ren's body double. Apparently requests for maintaining public order in various regions have gotten quite numerous.”
“Indeed. It seems there simply aren't enough soldiers to maintain order.”

“With the wave on top of worsening security, even on the slave trading side, we've been getting orders asking us to bind people with slave crests and supply them as soldiers for peacekeeping. The slave trader came to me directly with the request—wanting us to gather up demi-human and beastman slaves who look like they can fight.”

Was some kind of demand emerging, then? Bind them with slave crests, grant ownership to the soldiers, have the soldiers give orders from the rear while treating the slaves as expendable combatants—that sort of arrangement.
“Apparently the reason they wanted to buy Shion and the others was partly because they looked like capable fighters.”
“I've never heard of such a thing in any of the loops so far, I say.”

Was Melromarc short on soldiers? It wasn't as though this had never happened at all, but I'd never seen Melromarc so short-handed that it needed to conscript slaves as military force. Ah, but now that I thought of it, Father from the very first world had mentioned something about demi-humans and beastmen serving as soldiers in Melromarc. They'd come to Father's territory and had various friendly exchanges with him. Those from Éclair's territory to begin with, and then somehow through various interactions with people within Melromarc, ended up serving as soldiers, or something like that.

“Sounds pretty serious—apparently a fairly large proportion of people are being conscripted from every town and village… well, because of that, circus attendance has dropped quite a bit and we're starting to run a bit into the red.”
Father muttered this with a troubled look.
“According to what Motoyasu-kun and Rafumi-chan say, this kind of thing apparently doesn't happen in other loops… so what's causing it, I wonder.”
“I have no idea, I say.”
“Well… I don't think it's because of us, but apparently there was an incident where the soldiers and a general stationed at some fortress vanished overnight.”

“I've heard of that one. Back when I was still a fool, I was sent on a request to investigate it. According to survivors, it was a night of horror where people vanished one after another… apparently one of Mald's relatives was among them. Being related to Mald, he was apparently a pretty rotten sort of person too. Though Mald himself was the first to badmouth him.”
“So it wasn't just some sketchy friend-of-a-friend rumor—Itsuki was actually sent out on a request to investigate it… which means it really happened…”

Itsuki added, on reflection, that Smoked Meat hadn't seemed to feel much of anything about his vanished relative. So there had been an incident at some fortress like that. I knew nothing of it. Oh? In my memory, Father was pointing at me and shouting, You're the culprit, aren't you! But no, that wasn't it at all. That must have been a different fortress entirely, and on that occasion, I'd merely dealt out punishment to those scoundrels who'd tried to do Father harm.
